title: Laparoscopic pouch resizing vs endoscopic outlet repair of the gastrojejunostomy in patients with dumping syndrome after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a pilot trial
summary:
After gastric bypass surgery, a long-term complication known as dumping syndrome may occur. This condition develops when food passes too quickly from the stomach into the intestine after eating. It can lead to symptoms such as circulatory problems, discomfort, and significant fluctuations in blood sugar levels.

Studies have shown that there may be a connection between the development of dumping syndrome and an enlarged connection between the stomach and the small intestine. If this connection is too wide, food can leave the stomach and enter the intestine faster than intended.

If dietary changes and other non-surgical treatments do not provide sufficient improvement, different treatment options are available. These include both surgical procedures and treatments that can be performed without surgery using a gastroscopy. Both approaches aim to reduce the size of the connection between the stomach and the small intestine in order to slow down the passage of food.

To date, there are no scientific studies that directly compare these two treatment methods. Therefore, this pilot study will compare two approaches in patients who continue to experience symptoms after gastric bypass surgery: surgical reduction of the connection between the stomach and the small intestine and reduction of this connection using a procedure performed through gastroscopy.

The aim of this study is to determine whether the two treatment methods differ and whether one of the approaches offers advantages in treating significant blood sugar fluctuations after gastric bypass surgery.

The results of this pilot study will provide a basis for planning a larger study in which the two treatment methods can be compared under controlled conditions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age between 18 and 65 years
Patients who previously underwent a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass as a primary procedure for the treatment of obesity according to the currently accepted worldwide standard, with a 60 cm biliopancreatic limb and a 150 cm alimentary limb
Positive postoperative Sigstad score (>7 points)
Endoscopically measured diameter of the gastrojejunostomy of ≥2.5 cm
At least one pre-interventional postprandial hypoglycemic episode with a blood glucose level of <55 mg/dL during continuous glucose monitoring over a two-week period (late dumping syndrome)
Medical indication for interventional or surgical narrowing of the gastrojejunostomy for the treatment of dumping syndrome
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18 years or >65 years
Patients who underwent a surgical procedure differing from the standard Roux-en-Y gastric bypass described above
Previous bariatric surgery other than adjustable gastric banding
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
Language barrier preventing adequate information and understanding of the potential consequences of the treatment
Expected non-compliance
Patients with pre-existing diabetes mellitus prior to the initial Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery
Pregnancy
